---
title: "Plots with ggplot2 and tmap"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

A basemap goes under your data: `ggplot(nc) + m` in {ggplot2},
`tm_basemap(m)` in {tmap}. The plot gives what a basemap on its own needs
from you: the extent (the panel's limits), the CRS (the basemap is warped
into it, so it lines up with the data), the image size (the panel) and the
dpi (the device's: on screen 96, in `ggsave(dpi = 300)` 300, in PDF and SVG
300). It renders when the plot is drawn, so the preview and the export show
the same map, the export sharper, and credits the provider in the corner.

```{r}
library(tmap)        # before basemapper: basemapper's tm_basemap() replaces tmap's
library(basemapper)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
```

## ggplot2

Add a basemap to a plot like a layer. `geom_basemap()` does the same, taking
`basemap()`'s arguments:

```{r ggplot-choropleth}
ggplot(nc) +
  basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron") +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = SID79 / BIR79 * 1000), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_distiller("SIDS per 1,000\nbirths, 1979", palette = "OrRd", direction = 1) +
  theme_void()
```

### Projected data

The basemap is drawn in Web Mercator and warped into the plot's CRS, so it
lines up with data in any CRS. Here North Carolina's state plane
(EPSG:32119), with the counties' centroids:

```{r ggplot-projected}
nc_sp <- st_transform(nc, 32119)
centroids <- st_centroid(nc_sp)

ggplot(nc_sp) +
  basemap("Esri.WorldTopoMap") +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = centroids, aes(size = BIR74), colour = "#D96E34", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_size_area("Births, 1974", max_size = 6) +
  theme_void()
```

### A quieter basemap

For a data map, a basemap often reads better without its labels, faded, or
with only some of its features. Filters belong to the style (see [Stacking,
labels and features](layers.html)); `alpha` fades the layer:

```{r}
quiet <- style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = c("-labels", "-roads", "-rail"))

ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap(quiet, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = NWBIR74 / BIR74), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c("Share of births,\nnon-white, 1974", labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_void()
```

### More detail, or sharper

The plot fixes the extent and the image's pixels, so the zoom follows from
the dpi. A `zoom` of your own gives more (or less) detail: the dpi then
follows (an *effective dpi*, which basemapper reports once), and the style's
labels are drawn at that dpi.

```{r}
ggplot(nc) +
  basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", zoom = 8) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-80, -77.5), ylim = c(35, 36.5)) +
  theme_void()
```

The basemap follows the panel, so `coord_sf()` limits zoom it in, with
detail to match:

```{r}
ggplot(nc) +
  basemap("Esri.WorldImagery") +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "yellow", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = NAME), colour = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-76.9, -75.4), ylim = c(35.0, 36.0)) +
  theme_void()
```

### Clipping

`clip` draws the basemap only inside a layer's polygons, or outside them
with `outside()`. In a plot, the plot still gives the extent: the clip is a
mask. Here the state in colour over a faded copy (`alpha` belongs to the
layer, so the faded one is placed with `geom_basemap()`):

```{r}
ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap("Esri.WorldImagery", alpha = 0.35) +
  basemap("Esri.WorldImagery", clip = nc) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  theme_void()
```

### Credits

The credit line is on by default. `attribution = FALSE` turns it off;
`get_attribution()` returns the text, for a caption:

```{r}
gray <- basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas")

ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap(gray, attribution = FALSE) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(caption = get_attribution(gray)) +
  theme_void()
```

## tmap

`tm_basemap()` puts a basemap in a {tmap} v4 map; it takes a basemap, or a
style and `basemap()`'s arguments. tmap has a `tm_basemap()` of its own, so
attach tmap before basemapper (or call `basemapper::tm_basemap()`):

```{r}
tm_basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron") +
  tm_shape(nc) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "BIR79", fill_alpha = 0.75, col = "white", lwd = 0.5,
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.blues"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend("Births, 1979")
  )
```

The map is in the shapes' CRS, and the basemap is warped into it. Raster and
vector basemaps, stacks and filters work the same way; here shaded relief
under a vector basemap's labels, in the state plane:

```{r tmap-relief}
relief <- list("Esri.WorldShadedRelief", style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = "labels"))

tm_basemap(relief) +
  tm_shape(nc_sp) +
  tm_borders(col = "grey20", lwd = 0.6) +
  tm_dots(size = "BIR74", fill = "#D96E34", fill_alpha = 0.7, size.legend = tm_legend("Births, 1974"))
```

## Saving

`ggsave()` and `tmap_save()` render the basemap again at the file's dpi:
the same map, sharp at that resolution. A PDF or SVG gets it at 300 dpi.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ggsave("nc.png", width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
ggsave("nc.pdf", width = 7, height = 4)
```
